verifications.claim: The Pharisees were an influential Jewish social movement and school of thought in Palestine during the Second Temple period (c. 515 BCE–70 CE).
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R2: 'flourished in Palestine during the latter part of the Second Temple period (515 bce–70 ce)'; R5: 'Jewish social movement and school of thought in the Levant during the time of Second Temple Judaism'
verifications.reasoning: Direct match on description, location, and time period.

verifications.claim: The Pharisees adhered strictly to both written law and oral tradition.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R2: 'believed that the Law ... was twofold, consisting of the Written Law and the Oral Law'; R3: 'scrupulous observers of the Law as interpreted ... in accordance with tradition'
verifications.reasoning: Explicit support for adherence to both written and oral traditions.

verifications.claim: The Pharisees emphasized personal piety and ritual purity.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R2: 'society of scholars and pietists'; R3: 'one who separates himself ... from persons or things impure ... strict observance of Levitical purity'
verifications.reasoning: Direct references to piety and purity emphasis.

verifications.claim: The Pharisees believed in the resurrection of the dead, afterlife, and the existence of angels.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R3: 'resurrection of the body ... belief in angels and demons'; R4: 'believed in ... resurrection of the dead and the afterlife'; R5: 'resurrection of the dead ... belief in angels'
verifications.reasoning: All elements directly supported across sources.

verifications.claim: The Pharisees believed in the binding force of oral tradition, or the "unwritten Torah," alongside the written Mosaic law.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R2: 'insistence on the binding force of oral tradition ("the unwritten Torah")'
verifications.reasoning: Exact phrasing and concept match.

verifications.claim: The Pharisees believed in divine providence combined with human free will.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R3: 'Everything is foreseen ... but at the same time freedom is given'; R5: 'people have free will, but that God also has foreknowledge'
verifications.reasoning: Direct doctrinal match.

verifications.claim: The Pharisees believed in the immortality of the soul.
verifications.label: INCORRECT
verifications.evidence: R3: 'it was not the immortality of the soul which the Pharisees believed in, as Josephus puts it, but the resurrection of the body'
verifications.reasoning: Source explicitly corrects and contradicts the claim.

verifications.claim: The Pharisees were often middle-class.
verifications.label: VAGUE
verifications.evidence: R2: 'party of laymen and scribes in contradistinction to the Sadducees'; R5: 'in contrast to the more elite Sadducees ... Pharisees were ... more democratic'
verifications.reasoning: Implies non-aristocratic status but not explicitly 'middle-class'.

verifications.claim: The Pharisees were popular with the common people.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R2: 'enjoyed a large popular following'; R5: 'influence over the common people was so great ... backing and good-will of the common people'
verifications.reasoning: Explicit statements of popularity.

verifications.claim: The Pharisees served as leaders in synagogues.
verifications.label: VAGUE
verifications.evidence: R2: 'fostered the synagogue ... Pharasaic institution'; R3: 'institution of the synagogue ... Pharisaic declaration'
verifications.reasoning: They developed synagogues but not explicitly stated as leaders there.

verifications.claim: The strict school of Shammai and the more lenient school of Hillel.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R3: 'Shammaites ... Hillelites'; R5: 'schools of Hillel and Shammai'
verifications.reasoning: Sources describe the schools with strict (Shammai) and lenient (Hillel) characterizations.

verifications.claim: The Pharisees meticulously applied Levitical purity laws, originally meant for priests, to daily life and meals.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R3: 'precepts concerning unclean meat, intended originally for the priests only ... extended to the whole people ... same sanctity ... for their meals'
verifications.reasoning: Precise match on application of priestly purity laws to daily life.

verifications.claim: According to JewishEncyclopedia.com, the Pharisees were scrupulous about paying tithes and offering.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R3 (JewishEncyclopedia.com): 'scrupulous payment of tithes and other imposts due to the priest'
verifications.reasoning: Direct quote from specified source.

verifications.claim: The Pharisees emphasized study and interpretation of the law.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R2: 'use their reason in interpreting the Torah'; R3: 'Aristocracy of the Learned ... study of the Law'
verifications.reasoning: Clear emphasis on study and interpretation.

verifications.claim: The Pharisees shifted focus away from exclusive reliance on Temple sacrifices.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R2: 'worship consisted not in bloody sacrifices ... but in prayer and in the study of God’s law'; R3: 'spiritual life ... centered in the Torah and the Synagogue'
verifications.reasoning: Explicit shift to non-Temple worship.

verifications.claim: The Temple was destroyed in 70 AD.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R2: 'destruction of the Second Temple ... in 70 ce'; R5: 'destruction of the Second Temple in 70 AD'
verifications.reasoning: Exact date confirmed.

verifications.claim: After the Temple's destruction in 70 AD, Pharisaic beliefs became the foundation of Rabbinic Judaism.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R2: 'incorporated the teachings of the Pharisees on Jewish law'; R5: 'Pharisaic beliefs became the foundational ... basis for Rabbinic Judaism'
verifications.reasoning: Direct causal link post-destruction.

verifications.claim: In the New Testament, the Pharisees are often portrayed as opponents of Jesus due to their legalism and public hypocrisy.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'criticise the Pharisees for hypocrisy ... outward, ritual observance of minutiae'; R3: 'New Testament writings, which take a polemical attitude toward them'
verifications.reasoning: Matches NT portrayal of hypocrisy and legalism.

verifications.claim: Nicodemus was sympathetic to Jesus.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R5: 'Nicodemus the Pharisee (John 3:1) with Joseph of Arimathea entombed Jesus' body at great personal risk'
verifications.reasoning: Action implies sympathy, referenced from NT context.

verifications.claim: The Apostle Paul was an early follower of Jesus.
verifications.label: INCORRECT
verifications.evidence: R5: 'Paul the Apostle declared himself to be a Pharisee, even after his belief in Jesus'
verifications.reasoning: Paul converted post-crucifixion, not an early follower during Jesus' ministry.

verifications.claim: The Sadducees were aristocratic.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R2: 'party of the high priesthood'; R3: 'aristocracy of blood'; R5: 'Sadducees were aristocratic monarchists'
verifications.reasoning: Consistently described as aristocratic.

verifications.claim: The Sadducees only accepted the written Torah.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R2: 'refused to accept any precept as binding unless it was based directly on the Torah—i.e., the Written Law'; R4: 'rejected ... the Oral Torah'
verifications.reasoning: Exact doctrinal position.

verifications.claim: The Gospels often show conflict between the Pharisees and Jesus over ritual minutiae, such as fasting and Sabbath.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'outward, ritual observance of minutiae'; R5: 'healing a man's withered hand on Sabbath'
verifications.reasoning: Gospels' conflicts over rituals like Sabbath directly noted.

verifications.claim: In the Gospels, the Pharisees prioritized outward observance over internal righteousness.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'outwardly but left the inner person unreformed ... differences between inner and outer moral states'
verifications.reasoning: Precise description of Gospel portrayal.
